ai_language_tip: Speak natural Rioplatense-aware or neutral polite Spanish (es); understand voseo ('tenés/querés') and local terms ('turno', 'seña', 'remís'); English in BA Palermo/Punta del Este hotels.
english_ok: sometimes — Understood at upscale Buenos Aires, Mendoza winery, and Montevideo/Punta del Este venues, rarely at neighborhood shops.
politeness: Warm, conversational 'Hola, buen día / buenas tardes'; respectful usted or polite Rioplatense tone; close with 'muchas gracias, hasta luego'.
name_tip: First name and surname (e.g. Martín González); spell Italian/Basque/Eastern-European surnames clearly using city/common words.
phone_tip: AR 10-digit mobile 11 1234-5678 (locals sometimes still mention legacy '15'), UY mobile 099 123 456; read in pairs/blocks; WhatsApp dominates.
time_tip: 24-hour and 12-hour mixed ('21 hs' or 'nueve de la noche'); dinner is very late (21:00–23:30 — 20:00 is early!); 'menos cuarto' = :45.
number_tip: Aspirated 's' in Rioplatense makes dos/tres/seis softer; read phone blocks clearly (once, doce treinta y cuatro...).
avoid_calling: Avoid provincial siesta closure (~13:00–16:30 outside CABA/Montevideo center), late dinner rush 21:00–22:45, and calls before 09:00.
closed_days: Many restaurants/parrillas close Mondays (or Sunday nights); summer holiday migration in January slows Buenos Aires and peaks Punta del Este/Mar del Plata.
booking_channels: WhatsApp is king; Meitre, Woki, and TheFork for upscale dining; Docturno/DrApp and clinic WhatsApp bots for medical 'turnos'; PedidosYa for delivery.
voice_menu: Prepagas/Obras Sociales (OSDE, Swiss Medical, Mutualistas in UY), banks, ANSES/AFIP, telecoms, and couriers use heavy keypad IVR.
callback_habits: WhatsApp reconfirmation message day before or afternoon of booking is standard across restaurants, clinics, and salons.
